props.gloss_en: what [difference] is there between a limb from the living and a limb from a carcass?
flesh that separates from a limb from the living does not impart impurity
[flesh that separates] from a limb from a carcass imparts impurity
a limb from the living, which imparts impurity -- what is the verse?
Rav Yehuda said Rav said: 'and if [any] of the animal dies' (Lev 11:39)
'and if [any] of the animal dies' -- some of the animal imparts impurity and some does not; which is that? a tereifa that one slaughtered
it should not enter your mind [that flesh from the living imparts impurity]
might flesh separating from the living be impure? the verse says 'and if [any] of the animal dies' -- as death does not make a replacement, so all that does not make a replacement [imparts impurity]
R' Akiva: 'animal' -- as an animal is sinews and bones, so all that is sinews and bones
Rabbi: 'animal' -- as an animal is flesh, sinews and bones, so all that is flesh, sinews and bones
what [difference] is there between Rabbi and R' Akiva?
the knee joint is [the difference] between them
between R' Akiva and R' Yosei HaGelili, what is [the difference] between them?
Rav Pappa: the kidney and the lip are [the difference] between them
might flesh separating from sheratzim be impure? the verse says 'when they are dead' -- as death does not make a replacement, so all that does not make a replacement
R' Akiva: 'sheretz' -- as a sheretz is sinews and bones, so all that is sinews and bones
Rabbi: 'sheretz' -- as a sheretz is flesh, sinews and bones, so all that is flesh, sinews and bones
between Rabbi and R' Akiva the knee joint is [the difference]
between R' Akiva and R' Yosei HaGelili, what is [the difference] between them?
Rav Pappa: the kidney and the lip are [the difference] between them

had it taught us [only] the animal -- the reason it does not impart [impurity] from life would be that it does not impart in a lentil-bulk; but a sheretz, which imparts in a lentil-bulk, say it imparts from life

and had it taught us [only] the sheretz -- because it does not impart by carrying it does not impart from life; but an animal, which imparts by carrying, say it imparts from life. [Both are] necessary
one who severs an olive-bulk of flesh from a limb from the living -- severed it and afterwards designated it [as food] -- it is pure
designated it, and afterwards severed it -- it is impure
R' Asi to R' Zeira: what was said in the study hall?
R' Asi: it is impurity [by contact] in a concealed area, and impurity in a concealed area does not impart impurity
R' Abba bar Memel: whose is this [baraita]? it is R' Meir's
[R' Meir,] who said: impurity in a concealed area imparts impurity
R' Meir distinguishes between impurity that requires hechsher and impurity that does not require hechsher
Rava: and what is the difficulty? perhaps where it was rendered susceptible
Rabba bar Rav Chanan: why do I need hechsher? it imparts severe impurity by virtue of its father
Rava: when it served [as part of the limb], it served as wood
they said: a mass of leaven that one designated for sitting is nullified
Abaye: its impurity is not by Torah law
for if you thought it Torah law, we would have found foods that impart severe impurity
when it served [as a seat], it served as wood
they said: an idolatrous offering of foods imparts impurity in a tent
Abaye: its impurity is not by Torah law
for if you thought it Torah law, we would have found foods that impart severe impurity
when it served [as an offering], it served as wood
they said: connections of foods are like vessels
Abaye: their impurity is not by Torah law
for if you thought it Torah law, we would have found food that imparts severe impurity
when it served [as a connection], it served as wood
the baraita: carcass fat in the villages requires designation and hechsher
Rav Pappa: its impurity by virtue of the kidney is not by Torah law
for if you thought it Torah law, we would have found food that imparts severe impurity
when it served [the kidney], it served as wood
they said: a house that one roofed with seeds -- they became pure
Rav Mattana: its impurity is not by Torah law
for if you thought it Torah law, we would have found seeds that impart severe impurity
when they served [as a roof], they served as wood

answered_by.gloss_en: הא מני? רבי מאיר היא, דאמר טומאת בית הסתרים מטמיא (= p_abm_rabbi_meir; reported by R' Zeira)

objections.gloss_en: ולאו זימנין סגיאין אמרה קמאי, ואמרי ליה: שני ליה לרבי מאיר בין טומאה דבעיא הכשר ובין טומאה דלא בעיא הכשר
למה לי הכשר, הרי מטמא טומאה חמורה אגב אביו?
